analysis:
Examined both primary analyses and independently checked all replayed patches, metadata, declarations and tests. .github/workflows/release-desktop.yml:129 activates a fixed HTTPS GUI update feed; :173-192 retains release verification and adds embedded-feed and local artifact checks. Publication at :244-246 uploads the ZIP/blockmap before replacing the manifest. desktop-app/electron-builder.ts:27-31 now rejects release builds without a feed. desktop-app/scripts/update-feed.mjs:21-51 restamps post-signing metadata and verifies recognized entries against local hashes/sizes. Tests cover release feed requirements and HTTPS rejection. No supplied change alters inference encryption, authorization, attestation, billing, cache isolation or privileged-helper controls; no concrete regression is independently established.
The activated GUI executable-update channel implicates TB-003, T-013/T-043 and the distinction between signed artifacts and serving qualification in TB-011/T-054/A-017. Remaining material review: inspect desktop-app/src/main/{updates,updateFeed}.ts for runtime signature/identity enforcement and safe installation during native operations. These controls are outside the replayed evidence, not observed missing controls. Confirm whether runtime selection ignores the advertised versioned DMG, since publication uploads a versionless DMG; local hash checking does not verify the remote asset set. Also verify ordering of concurrent publications to the shared manifest and whether stale publication can suppress security updates. Neither runtime selection nor downgrade behavior is established here, so these are questions rather than findings.
Replay is incomplete (18 source units omitted), including documentation/source excerpts underlying several prior conclusions. Human review should reconcile those excerpts and document GUI feed authority separately from native serving qualification; this review does not establish a threat-model omission or qualify the full PR.
